report: Read all ten candidate groups end to end against the six verses. None is a split: every difference is one the ASV's own English licenses.

הוּא: PSA.128.2 gives *thy* to the possessive suffix on `כַּפֶּיךָ` and *thou* to the subject suffix on `אַשְׁרֶיךָ`; each is the pronoun the ASV wrote, under rule 18. Every other suffix in the chapter takes its written possessive or object pronoun.

בְּ / לְ: 128.1 and 128.3 write *in*/*In* for the preposition; 128.5 promotes `בְּטוּב` to the direct object of *see* and is `unrepresented` under rule 40; 128.3's `סָבִיב לְ` is `unrepresented` because *Round about* is wholly the adverb's; 128.6's periphrastic-genitive `לְבָנֶיךָ` fuses into *children's* under rules 30/49's closing sentence, the possessive marker standing on a word that would otherwise be bare and the suffix keeping its own *thy*. Four different English facts, four treatments — consistent.

וְ: *And* (128.5) and *Yea* (128.6) are both written connectives under rule 14. כְּ: 128.3a writes the copula (*shall be as*, on the preposition under rule 49) and 128.3b gaps it (*like*); rules 34/49 place only what is written. כִּי: *For* (128.2) is written, `הִנֵּה כִי־כֵן` → *Behold thus* (128.4) spends nothing on it. כֹּל: *every one* (128.1, generic joined under rule 31) vs *all* (128.5). אֶשֶׁר and בָּרַךְ differ only in the ASV's copula/auxiliary shape.
The two `יְרֵא יְהוָה` phrases (128.1, 128.4) agree: `יְרֵא` takes *that/That feareth* and `יְהוָה` the bare object in both.
BSB disagreements (128.3 לְ, 128.5 בְּ, 128.4 כִי) are all documented convention differences — BSB attaches a silenced preposition or particle to its phrase — and none is an error.

The five repeated review notes the validator lists restate contract rules (18, 19, 25, 40) and need no convention. Nothing here generalises beyond what the contract already says; no promotions or amendments.
